pattern.short_summary: One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role.
pattern.definition: One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role. The asymmetry is designed rather than incidental: some information is withheld from one side, or an extra channel exists for the other. The parties nonetheless act on a shared underlying state.
pattern.structural_signature: A single backend serves two or more role-specific front-ends or channels whose contents differ by construction; a role assignment determines which view a session receives; at least one channel is private to one role. State written by any role is visible to the others only through their own role's view.

dimension.category_description: How human and artificial participants are personified, assigned visible roles, coordinated, simulated, or represented to one another.
dimension.classification_boundary: Identity or social organization must be user-facing; invisible multi-agent division of labor is excluded.
